# FDG8019

> AVOID using `ICollection<T>` or `ICollection` as a parameter just to access the `Count` property.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.3.1 Collection Parameters.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Analyzer candidate rejected: telling that a parameter is used only for its Count needs every use of the parameter, including the members it is passed to; a parameter passed on to a member that needs ICollection<T> must keep the type.

## From the book

Instead, consider using `IEnumerable<T>` or `IEnumerable` and dynamically checking whether the object implements `ICollection<T>` or `ICollection`.

```csharp
public List(IEnumerable<T> collection){
   // check if it implements ICollection
   if (collection is ICollection<T> col) {
      this.Capacity = collection.Count;
   }

   foreach(T item in collection){
      Add(item);
   }
}
```
